answer.evidence: radon/metrics.py:150-157 defines mi_rank(score): `chr(65 + (9 - score >= 0) + (19 - score >= 0))`. The docstring says A if score > 19, B if 9 < score <= 19, C if score <= 9. Score <= 9 gives both terms 1, so 'C'. Score 10–19 gives one term, so 'B'. Score > 19 gives 'A'. The boundaries 9 and 19 are inclusive for the lower grade. mi_compute (line 98) produces the score. radon/complexity.py is a secondary file because it has a separate letter-grade mapping for cyclomatic complexity. radon/raw.py and radon/visitors.py have no MI grading. I did not open the handoff_refs files; I treated them as ordinary context.
